title: SEO
hired_for: To win buyers who search for what we sell, without paying for each click: rank for the terms that sell, keep pages in Google and protect what already ranks.

jobs.job: Catch an organic sales drop within a week and name the cause
jobs.why: Organic drops are quiet. A theme update that blocks Google or a lost ranking on one money page can cost weeks of sales before anyone looks.

watch.metric: non-brand organic revenue, 28 day, versus the same period last year
watch.source: GA4 organic sessions joined to Shopify orders

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: non-brand organic revenue fell 22% and no one knew why. After: the drop is traced to 3 collection pages set to noindex in a theme update, fixed in 2 days.

jobs.job: Fix what stops Google from finding and indexing our money pages
jobs.why: A product or collection page that is not in Google cannot rank or sell. Blocked pages, broken links and wrong canonical tags hide pages without warning.

watch.metric: share of submitted product and collection pages that are indexed, 28 day
watch.source: Google Search Console page indexing report

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 81% of money pages indexed, 60 collection pages excluded as duplicates. After: 97% indexed within 4 weeks.

jobs.job: Protect rankings through site changes and migrations
jobs.why: A new theme, new URLs or a platform move can wipe out years of rankings in a week if redirects and page content are not carried over.

watch.metric: organic clicks 28 days after a site change versus the 28 days before, and redirect errors found
watch.source: Google Search Console and a site crawl (Screaming Frog, Sitebulb)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a theme change is planned with no redirect map. After: every old URL maps to a live page and clicks hold within 5% of before.

jobs.job: Decide if SEO is worth the spend this quarter
jobs.why: SEO takes months to pay back. If the category has little search demand or thin margin, the money is better spent elsewhere.

watch.metric: search demand for the terms we sell times gross margin per order (proxy: monthly search volume and impressions)
watch.source: Google Keyword Planner and Google Search Console

drives.metric: planned organic gross profit for the quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $4,000 a month on SEO with no case. After: 90,000 monthly searches on 40 money terms justify it, with a 6-month revenue check set.

jobs.job: Get money pages onto page 1 for the terms that sell
jobs.why: Pages sitting at positions 8 to 20 get few clicks. Pushing them into the top 5 is the fastest organic growth because Google already trusts them.

watch.metric: share of money terms where our page ranks in the top 10, 28 day
watch.source: Google Search Console average position by query

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 14 of 60 money terms (23%) on page 1. After: better titles, content and internal links bring 25 of 60 (42%) onto page 1 in 3 months.

jobs.job: Make our collection pages the best answer for the category
jobs.why: Category searches like 'wool hiking socks' are where most buyers start. A bare product grid with no help loses to competitors that explain and compare.

watch.metric: non-brand organic clicks to collection pages, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 3 of 12 collection pages have any text or FAQ. After: all 12 do, and collection clicks rise 30% in 3 months.

jobs.job: List every product in Google's free Shopping listings
jobs.why: Free listings put products with price and image in Google Shopping at no cost per click. A missing or broken product feed leaves that traffic to competitors.

watch.metric: clicks from free product listings, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 40% of products rejected for missing fields. After: 98% approved, free listing clicks up 3x.

jobs.job: Refresh pages whose clicks are falling before writing new ones
jobs.why: Pages that used to earn money slowly decay as competitors update. Refreshing a proven page is faster and cheaper than ranking a new one.

watch.metric: clicks to pages that fell 20% or more over 90 days, 28 day

drives.metric: organic revenue at risk from falling pages

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 8 pages earning $5,000 a month have lost 30% of clicks. After: refreshed pages regain most of it in 6 weeks.

jobs.job: Get more clicks from pages that already show up in search
jobs.why: A page seen thousands of times but rarely clicked is wasted ranking. A better title and description can lift clicks without any ranking change.

watch.metric: click rate versus what the page's position should earn, top 50 pages by impressions, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the hero product page gets 2% of clicks at position 3. After: a rewritten title reaches 7%.

jobs.job: Keep ranking pages alive when a product is discontinued or out of stock
jobs.why: Deleting a ranking product page throws away its links and traffic. Pointing it to a similar product keeps the buyer and the ranking.

watch.metric: former product URLs that return 'not found' while still getting search clicks or links
watch.source: Google Search Console and a site crawl

drives.metric: organic revenue kept from retired products

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 22 retired product pages return 'not found'. After: each redirects to the closest live product.

jobs.job: Keep our own brand and product names at position 1
jobs.why: People searching our name are ready to buy. Losing that spot to a reseller, marketplace or review site costs easy sales.

watch.metric: position for brand and brand-plus-product searches, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: Amazon outranks us for 'brand name plus product' on 4 products. After: our pages hold position 1 on all 4.

jobs.job: Make sure analytics count organic sales correctly
jobs.why: Broken tags or missing Search Console access make organic look better or worse than it is, and budget follows the wrong number.

watch.metric: organic orders in GA4 versus matched Shopify orders, 28 day

drives.metric: trust in the organic revenue number

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: GA4 records 70% of Shopify orders. After: fixed tags record 95%.

jobs.job: Screen an SEO or link vendor pitch before signing
jobs.why: SEO vendors sell with big numbers. Checking their claim against our own data avoids paying for work that cannot move sales.

watch.metric: vendor claim versus our own Search Console and GA4 numbers for the same pages

drives.metric: SEO spend with no measured return

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a vendor promises 300% traffic growth. After: our data shows the terms they target have 200 searches a month, and the deal is dropped.

jobs.job: Link money pages from content and fix pages nothing links to
jobs.why: Pages with no internal links look unimportant to Google and buyers cannot find them. Links from guides pass trust to the pages that sell.

watch.metric: money pages with fewer than 3 internal links, and pages with no internal links

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 18 money pages get no links from any guide. After: every guide links to its matching collection, 0 orphans.

jobs.job: Keep product data markup valid so listings show price, stock and stars
jobs.why: Search results with stars, price and stock get more clicks. Broken markup quietly removes them.

watch.metric: product pages with valid product and review markup versus pages with errors, 28 day

drives.metric: click rate from search to product pages

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 45 product pages show markup errors, no stars in results. After: 0 errors, stars show on all of them.

jobs.job: Get seasonal pages ranking before the season starts
jobs.why: Pages need weeks to rank. A holiday or seasonal page published the week of the peak misses most of the demand.

watch.metric: impressions on seasonal pages 6 weeks before the peak

drives.metric: organic revenue in the seasonal window

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the gift guide goes live 1 week before Black Friday. After: it is refreshed in September and ranks on page 1 by November.

jobs.job: Write product pages the way shoppers search
jobs.why: Product titles in brand language miss the words buyers type. Plain names, real facts and clear photos win the long, specific searches.

watch.metric: non-brand impressions and clicks to product pages, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 'The Voyager' ranks for nothing. After: 'Voyager merino hiking sock, cushioned' earns 3,000 impressions a month.

jobs.job: Stop two of our pages competing for the same term
jobs.why: When 2 pages chase the same search, Google splits the signal and both rank worse.

watch.metric: money terms where 2 or more of our pages get impressions, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 9 terms split between a collection and a blog post. After: each term has one page, and 6 move up.

jobs.job: Keep thin and duplicate pages out of Google
jobs.why: Tag pages, filter pages and duplicate product URLs use up Google's attention and can outrank the real page.

watch.metric: indexed pages that are not money or content pages (tags, filters, duplicates)
watch.source: Google Search Console page indexing report

drives.metric: share of indexed pages that are money pages

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1,400 tag and filter pages indexed next to 300 real pages. After: under 50.

jobs.job: Set the site structure before adding more pages
jobs.why: If the collection tree and URLs do not match how buyers search, new content has nowhere good to point and pages compete.

watch.metric: money terms mapped to exactly one target page
watch.source: keyword map in the brand brain checked against Google Search Console

drives.metric: count of money terms ranking in the top 10

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 30% of money terms have a clear target page. After: 90% do, after 6 new collections are added.

jobs.job: Write guides and comparisons that lead buyers to a money page
jobs.why: Buyers who are still choosing search for comparisons and advice. A guide that answers them and links to the product catches the buyer early.

watch.metric: organic visits to guides that go on to a product or collection page, 90 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 20 lifestyle posts, 1% click through to a product. After: 5 buyer guides, 12% click through.

jobs.job: Earn links from sites our buyers read
jobs.why: Links from real, relevant sites tell Google the store is trusted. Bought or junk links can bring a penalty.

watch.metric: new referring domains per month from relevant sites
watch.source: Google Search Console links report or a backlink tool (Ahrefs, Semrush)

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 0 new relevant links in 3 months. After: expert answers to journalists bring 4 a month.

jobs.job: Give each country its own pages when selling in more than one
jobs.why: One page for all countries shows the wrong price, currency or shipping to half the buyers, and Google may show the wrong version.

watch.metric: organic clicks and revenue by country, 28 day
watch.source: Google Search Console by country and GA4

drives.metric: organic revenue outside the home market

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: UK buyers land on US prices. After: a UK version ranks in the UK and UK organic revenue doubles.
